record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.context_brief: Sampling lattice points in convex bodies
record.original_question: Can one sample lattice points in a convex body under substantially weaker geometric assumptions than the currently known large-inscribed-ball condition? For example, is efficient sampling possible for lattice points of a near-isotropic convex body, or for a body that contains at least half of a ball of radius O(sqrt(n))?

evidence.quote: Can this condition be improved substantially? E.g., can one sample lattice points of a near-isotropic convex body? Or lattice points of a body that contains at least half of a ball of radius O(√n)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body presented by a well-guaranteed membership oracle, and let $\mathbb{Z}^n$ denote the integer lattice. Existing polynomial-time algorithms can sample (approximately uniformly) from $K \cap \mathbb{Z}^n$ provided $K$ contains a Euclidean ball of "large" radius (for example, radius polynomial in $n$ with appropriate constants), an assumption substantially stronger than what is required for sampling continuous points in $K$.

A convex body $K$ of volume $1$ is said to be in near-isotropic position if its centroid is at the origin and its covariance matrix $\frac{1}{\mathrm{vol}(K)}\int_K x x^\top\,dx$ is close (say within a constant factor in the Loewner order) to the identity $I_n$.

Question: Determine whether there exists a randomized algorithm that, given oracle access to a convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, samples from a distribution within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the uniform distribution on $K \cap \mathbb{Z}^n$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n, \log(1/\varepsilon))$ under either of the following weakened geometric hypotheses:

(a) $K$ is in near-isotropic position (with no additional inscribed-ball assumption); or

(b) $K$ contains at least half of some Euclidean ball of radius $O(\sqrt{n})$, i.e., there exists a ball $B$ of radius $c\sqrt{n}$ such that $\mathrm{vol}(K \cap B) \ge \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{vol}(B)$.

Either provide such an algorithm, or prove that no such algorithm exists (e.g., under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions).
artifact.category_tag: Lattice point sampling in convex bodies
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface the Kannan–Vempala framework for sampling lattice points (STOC 1997) and subsequent surveys on algorithmic convex geometry, but no result has been found that relaxes the large-inscribed-ball condition to mere near-isotropy or to the half-of-an-$O(\sqrt n)$-ball condition. Recent work on sampling/volume in convex bodies focuses on the continuous setting (e.g., the KLS conjecture, isotropic rounding complexity), and the lattice-point version under weakened geometric hypotheses appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: High-dimensional Sampling Algorithms (Vempala)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of sampling algorithms emphasizing isotropic transformation as a bottleneck; lattice-point sampling under relaxed conditions not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: No improved algorithm under weaker geometric assumptions is reported in subsequent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including relaxing the geometric condition for sampling lattice points in a convex body.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in algorithmic convex geometry.

status_evidence.title: Lattice Points and Lattice Polytopes (Handbook chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys algorithmic results on lattice points; does not provide a sampling algorithm under near-isotropy alone.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the weakened-hypothesis lattice-point sampling problem is recorded in the handbook.
